# oflh (Open File Lock Handle)

> Cross-platform tool that shows which processes are using a file, folder, or local port, and lets you close or terminate them safely. Interactive terminal app (`oflh`) and desktop app (OFLH Desktop) for Windows, Linux, and macOS on x86-64 and ARM64. Written in Rust, MIT licensed.

Key facts:

- Finds file users by enumerating process references (open descriptors/handles, memory mappings, loaded modules, executables, working directories), not by walking directories, so whole-drive scans (`oflh 'C:\'`, `oflh /`) take well under a second on the recorded machines.
- Usage: `oflh [OPTIONS] [PATH]`. Options: `--ports`, `--port PORT`, `--language en|de|zh|system`, `--no-update-check`, `--version`, `--help`. Options go before PATH.
- The CLI is interactive only: it requires a TTY and has no JSON or script output mode.
- "Open" is not "locked": lock evidence is reported separately (Linux flock/POSIX/OFD locks, macOS F_GETLK conflicts, Windows sharing violations with the owner marked unverified).
- Process actions verify PID plus start time before signaling and never close handles inside another process.
- Ports: local TCP listeners and bound UDP sockets only, read from OS socket tables without running lsof, ss, or netstat.
